It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. div.head: ECf 32 C 1a
div.ab: Saxones uero Germanie cum ueniunt in regno, suscipi debent et protegi in regno isto sicut coniurati fratres nostri et sicut proprii ciues regni huius: exierunt enim quondam de sanguine Anglorum, scilicet de Engra ciuitate, et Anglici de sanguine illorum, et semper efficiuntur populus unus et gens una.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 658 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 C …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

note.seg: Gefühl des Bundes der Welfen mit Heinrich II. und seinen Söhnen oder Abbild des wirklichen damaligen Vorrechtes Norddeutscher Händler; vgl. IV Atr. 2, 8; Höhlbaum III S. 281; n. 59. 63. 69. 110
a sense of the alliance of the Welfs with Henry II and his sons, or a reflection of the real privilege of North German traders at that time; cf. IV Atr. 2, 8; Höhlbaum III p. 281; n. 59. 63. 69. 110
sicut homines proprii werden Fremde begünstigt in Freibriefen, so seit 1157 Cölner; Höhlbaum Hansisch. Urk. I S. 8. 16. 22
foreigners are favoured sicut homines proprii in charters, so from 1157 the men of Cologne; Höhlbaum, Hansisch. Urk. I pp. 8. 16. 22

der Londoner meint das Land Angeln, ihm (mittelbar) aus Bæda’s Angulus bekannt. Er verderbte den Namen vielleicht durch phonetische Orthographie des Anlauts, vielleicht aber zog er auch confus Engern, das Land an der Weser heran, worüber Norddeutsche erzählen mochten

the Londoner means the land of Angeln, known to him (indirectly) from Bede’s Angulus. He perhaps corrupted the name through a phonetic spelling of the initial, but perhaps he also confusedly drew in Engern, the land on the Weser, of which North Germans may have told
Connubium als Mittel zur Einung der Nation auch 32 C 4 ff. E 2. Ludwig IX. precepit ut federe maritali Franci Normannis concatenarentur; Math. Paris. ebd. 370
connubium as a means of uniting the nation also at 32 C 4 ff. and E 2. Louis IX precepit ut federe maritali Franci Normannis concatenarentur; Math. Paris., ibid. 370

div.ab: The Saxons of Germany, when they come into the kingdom, ought to be received and protected in this kingdom as our sworn brothers and as own citizens of this kingdom: for they went out once from the blood of the English, namely from the city of Engra, and the English from their blood, and they always become one people and one nation.
